title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: An employee of the Group, including all Directors and Senior Management, plus a company or trust controlled by a Director or Senior Manager and their spouse, child, close relative (if acting in concert) or financially dependent person. Subject to the general insider trading prohibition (clause 3).

tiers.name: Tivan Person
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management, persons who work closely with them or in the finance/strategy team, IT staff with access to sensitive materials, other employees who may possess market sensitive information, and any other person the Board designates in writing; also includes a controlled company or trust and (for clause 4 purposes only) a spouse, child, close relative or financially dependent/acting-in-concert person. This is the population subject to Blackout Periods, protection-arrangement, margin lending/security and notification rules.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board or Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board or the Chief Executive Officer, distinguished only for the identity of their Authorising Officer (an Independent Director) when seeking consent to deal.

tiers.name: Other Directors, Company Secretary and Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, the Company Secretary, and any other Key Management Personnel; distinguished only for the identity of their Authorising Officer (the Chair, or in his/her absence an Independent Director).

tiers.name: Any other Tivan Person
tiers.description: Tivan Persons other than the Chair/CEO or other directors, Company Secretary and KMP; distinguished only for the identity of their Authorising Officer (the Company Secretary, or in his/her absence the CEO).

tiers.name: Independent Director
tiers.description: A non-executive director of the Company; appears only as the Authorising Officer for the Chair's or CEO's dealings.

definitions.hedging_definition: operate to limit the economic risk of any Tivan Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Tivan's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Tivan Person's behalf

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Tivan may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading in Tivan's securities by any or all Tivan Persons (and other Employees), even where the proposed trade would otherwise be outside a Blackout Period. Any restriction communicated under this power must be kept strictly confidential.

rules.detail: Securities is defined to include options and other securities, and 'financial products or securities' cannot be dealt in during a Blackout Period. Non-speculative derivatives dealing that is not a protection arrangement is a Dealing requiring Authorising Officer consent and must occur outside a Blackout Period; short-term or speculative derivatives dealing is banned outright under 5.1.
rules.evidence: During Blackout Periods Company Persons must not deal in any of Tivan's financial products or securities, or in any securities related to them.

rules.detail: Protection arrangements, expressly including hedging arrangements that limit the economic risk of a holding, are prohibited outright over unvested Tivan securities.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Tivan securities (or Tivan products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tivan securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The same outright ban on protection/hedging arrangements applies to vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tivan securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Once vested and free of any holding lock, hedging arrangements (an expressly named example of a protection arrangement) may be entered into with the Authorising Officer's consent under clause 4.3.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under clause 4.3. ... operate to limit the economic risk of any Tivan Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements)

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are named as an example of derivative-market transactions; short-term or speculative CFD trading is banned outright, but non-speculative CFD dealing is a Dealing requiring Authorising Officer consent (and is a protection arrangement, subject to 5.2, if it limits risk or enables profit from a price fall).

rules.detail: Margin lending arrangements involving unvested Tivan securities are banned outright.
rules.evidence: Tivan Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tivan securities.

rules.detail: The same ban applies to securities subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: Tivan Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Tivan securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tivan securities.

rules.evidence: Unless clause 5.3(a) applies, Tivan Persons may, directly or indirectly ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Tivan securities, with consent under clause 4.3.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security (charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over unvested Tivan securities, to secure any obligation of the Tivan Person or a third party, is banned outright.

rules.detail: No fixed period; an absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading, including short-term direct dealing and short-term/speculative derivative transactions.

What constitutes "exceptional circumstances" will be assessed on a case-by-case basis within the absolute discretion of the Authorising Officer, and may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship
or a requirement to comply with a court order or court enforceable undertaking.

exemption_authority: In exceptional circumstances (including, without limitation, severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking) the Authorising Officer may, in absolute discretion and without giving reasons, approve dealing in Tivan securities during a Blackout Period or other dealing otherwise prohibited by the policy (clause 4.4); such clearance can be withdrawn if new information emerges or circumstances change, is final and binding, and must be kept strictly confidential. Separately, the Board (clause 4.2) may impose additional, confidential ad hoc trading restrictions at its sole and absolute discretion at any time, even outside a Blackout Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Tivan securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and (b) otherwise, requires consent under clause 4.3.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Once the executive's shares are vested and free of any holding lock, both the derivative legs and the secured loan of a funded collar move from an absolute ban to a clearance-based regime, making the structure achievable in principle post-vesting.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Tivan securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excluded from the policy altogether, so it is not a breach and is not blocked by a Blackout Period or the notification regime - a materially more collar-friendly enforcement position than policies that treat lender enforcement as a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt and without limiting the generality of this policy, entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: (a) amount to "short selling" ...; (b) operate to limit the economic risk ...; or (c) otherwise enable a Tivan Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is purposive and would clearly catch a purchased put and written call as a collar, regardless of how the bank documents or labels the trade.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Tivan may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading in Tivan's securities ... Any restriction communicated ... must be kept strictly confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, unwind or roll of the collar can be blocked at any time by an undisclosed restriction, creating timing risk the bank cannot see coming or verify.

bespoke_clauses.topic: clearance revocable and voided by later inside information
bespoke_clauses.clause: can be withdrawn (if clearance has been given) if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances ... If a Tivan Person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving a clearance to trade, they must not trade despite having received the clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade or its financing can become unexecutable between approval and execution/settlement if inside information arises or the Authorising Officer withdraws consent.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy once the executive's shares are vested and free of any holding lock, but not before. Clause 5.2 bans all 'protection arrangements' (expressly including hedging, short selling beyond holding, and profiting from a price fall - covering a put/call collar) outright while shares are unvested or holding-locked, and clause 5.3 imposes the same absolute ban on granting security or margin lending over such shares; once vested and unrestricted, both the derivative legs and a secured loan may proceed with the consent of the Authorising Officer (an Independent Director, the Chair, or the Company Secretary/CEO depending on the requester's role) obtained before dealing and outside a Blackout Period, with a post-trade confirmation required. Notably, clause 6(a)(viii) excludes from the policy altogether 'a disposal of Tivan securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement', so the bank's enforcement sale on default is not itself a breach. Constraints that remain even post-vesting include the quarterly/half-year/full-year/AGM Blackout Periods (with Exceptional Circumstances relief available only in the Authorising Officer's absolute discretion), the Board's power to impose confidential ad hoc restrictions at any time, and the fact that a clearance can be withdrawn or voided if inside information arises before completion.
